{"notes": "Visit 2 (left at 5:30). Picture: the top body curve is now complete and dark from the nose to the tail join, so the main risk from visit 1 is closed. The bottom curve and both tail lobes are dark and connected. Two pale loose dominoes sit at the tail join, and Tom says they are tucked inside, off the chain. They look harmless but are worth a glance at the push. No hands were on the table when I left, and the team had agreed to keep off it.

Tom: At 5:15 he checked the whole fish from his side and confirmed it lit up from nose to both tail lobes. He spotted the two loose dominoes and made a sensible call to leave them alone. He also credited Leo and called hands off. Good verification, calm judgment and positive team behavior. His bottom curve was strong from visit 1. Still no direct view of his building.

Maya: At 5:00 she checked both tail lobes from her side, thanked Leo, and called for hands off to avoid bumps. Good risk awareness and collaboration. The top curve is now complete and was her task, but I didn't see her finish it, so I'm crediting the result with caution.

Leo: Maya thanked him by name for the tail lobes, and Tom echoed it. That points to real contribution, but I still haven't seen who laid the upper lobe, so I'm treating it as likely, not confirmed. I never saw the right-end join check he promised.

Priya: Silent this visit, so no new evidence. Her early tail split and her lower lobe still stand as good initiative and clear communication.

Before ratings: ask each person privately who laid the upper lobe, who finished the top curve, and who did the join check. Then watch the push result."}
